scope: Read-only adversarial engineering review of draft context and companion identity retirement. Private isolated React/jsdom reproduction; no native UI, login, model, operational record or aircraft action.

review_findings.severity: Availability and draft continuity; no established cross-tenant disclosure
review_findings.finding: Render-time mutation of a shared ref invalidates the still-committed actor A draft setter when a concurrent actor B render suspends without committing.
review_findings.reproduction: startTransition requests B; B calls useDraftState then suspends forever. A remains displayed. Editing A expects A after but received A before.
review_findings.test_framework: Vitest4.1.12, React, jsdom; existing installed locked dependencies
review_findings.related_code_review: CompanionDock has a related render-time boundary ref mutation; analogous abandoned-render behavior is a code-review concern, not separately reproduced here.
review_findings.resolution: Reported immediately to root and draft owner; owner will fix and rerun regression tests.

reviewed_scenarios: Committed A to B to A scope tokens and stale direct/functional setters
Async conversation creation stops follow-up on retired session
Token or role change keyed session remount
Storage read/write failure remains in memory without wrong-key carryover
Distinct mock sent-message IDs fix a test fixture duplicate-key warning without changing product behavior
limitations: Normal App sign-out clears local session/drafts and unmounts the companion. No production exploit across normal sign-out was demonstrated.
Current App has no Suspense/startTransition identity-change path found in the reviewed source.
This is a bounded source/test review, not operational acceptance, domain certification, full security assurance or proof of absence of other defects.
No full suite was rerun by this reviewer; root owns the concurrent integration run.
The private harness initially failed configuration import resolution; explicit installed config.js import repaired the harness before the actual failing test.
